$comment: The feature atlas (docs/PLAN.md 5.10). One entry per observable feature; ids are never reused. `factory compile` creates planned entries; the PR that completes a feature sets 'built' and lists its tagged tests. Checked by `npm run factory -- atlas`.

features.name: API routes are protected by default
features.description: Every /api route requires credentials unless its method and path are on the explicit public list (today GET /api/v1/health); a public endpoint not on the list cannot be defined; a test enumerates the served route tree.

features.name: OpenAPI document, generated client and breaking-change check
features.description: packages/api-client/openapi.json and src/schema.ts generated from the endpoint contracts and checked for staleness; CI fails a breaking change unless a spec in the PR declares contract_impact api-major.

features.name: Room status passthrough and CORS for the reader's origins
features.description: GET /api/v1/rooms/{roomId}/status from the relay with timeout, retry and fallback; CORS from SOCIAL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

features.name: Call token endpoint for room members
features.description: POST /api/v1/rooms/{roomId}/call/token: a member gets a 10-minute LiveKit token for that room only, identity u:<user id>, role in metadata, publish microphone, camera and screen share, no data; 404 for non-members and missing rooms alike, 401 without identity. Rate limited to 20 per user and room per minute (429 with retry-after); tokens and LiveKit secrets never logged.

features.name: LiveKit webhooks, call status, and deletion leaving calls
features.description: POST /api/v1/internal/livekit/webhook verified with the LiveKit secret, idempotent on the event id, keeps call_status (live, participants) per room; a deleted account is removed from every live call through LiveKit, a failure retried once and logged without stopping the deletion.

features.name: Owner mutes or removes a call participant
features.description: POST .../call/mute and .../call/remove, owner only (403 member, 404 outsider, 503 when calls are off), through LiveKit server API; removal keeps them in the room and refuses their call tokens for 15 minutes (call_removals).

features.name: Recordings API: start, upload, list, read and delete a session recording
features.description: POST /api/v1/rooms/:roomId/recordings starts a recording for the room's owner, whose browser uploads numbered media chunks and the state track and finishes it with its duration; members list and read a room's recordings, and its recorder or the room's owner deletes one.

features.name: Broadcasts API: start, end, relay tickets and view-only call grants
features.description: POST /api/v1/rooms/:roomId/broadcasts (the owner only, one live per room) and POST /api/v1/broadcasts/:id/end, GET a broadcast, a 10-minute HMAC relay ticket naming the broadcast, the user and their role (host or viewer), and a LiveKit token for bcast_<id> that lets the host publish and a viewer only subscribe, hidden.

features.name: Feed API: live, scheduled and recent for the viewer
features.description: GET /api/v1/feed: the viewer's live rooms (relay status with ref, heRef, title, count), upcoming shiurim they may attend, and their other rooms; 200 with everything recent when the relay is down.

features.name: Light card: article with one stretched link and status in words
features.description: A card per room or shiur: an article labelled by its heading, one stretched link to the lobby or shiur page, status from the server's read in words, the ref in the interface language; checked visually in English, Hebrew and dark.

features.name: Source-text renderer from the public text API
features.description: ui/SourceText.tsx: validated, plain-text only (no markup from the API), Hebrew and English blocks with lang and dir, a fallback line on failure.

features.name: Enlarge from a card with a view transition
features.description: Pressing a live card enlarges into the room (R9) with the card's ref as fallback target; view transition where supported, transform and clip-path otherwise, none with reduced motion; modified clicks stay links.

features.name: Feed page at /social
features.description: Live now, Scheduled and Recent sections of cards; signed-out prompt with the reader's sign-in; error alert; polls every 30 s; both interface languages.

features.name: A feed of live cards opens no sockets
features.description: No WebSocket and no reader for cards until a press or an enlarge; counted in component tests and end to end.

features.name: Prefetch on visibility and on press
features.description: A card's text is fetched only within 200px of the viewport, once per ref; pressing a live card prepares the room's session (prefetch hold, released after 10 s).

features.name: Posts with an optional source, written as a person or an institution
features.description: POST /api/v1/posts stores a 1–2,000 character Torah thought, optionally anchored to a source citation, as the viewer's own profile or an institution they administer (403 otherwise).

features.name: The timeline: Following and Everyone, newest first, in pages
features.description: GET /api/v1/timeline answers the posts of followed profiles and the viewer's own (tab=following) or everyone's, 20 a page with a keyset cursor, each with author, counts and the viewer's reaction; deleted posts never appear.

features.name: A post's own page and deleting a post
features.description: GET /api/v1/posts/{postId} with its replies; DELETE by its author or an institution administrator; /social/p/$postId shows the post, its source and actions, with confirmation before deleting and social's not-found message for an unknown id.

features.name: The composer and the timeline on /social
features.description: The home page: a composer that invites a Torah thought with a source pre-filled from the reader, Post as, a character count near the limit, and the Following/Everyone timeline with skeletons, Show more and an empty state; Hebrew-first, relative times, keyboard tabs.

features.name: Replies under a post
features.description: POST /api/v1/posts/{postId}/replies and DELETE /api/v1/replies/{replyId} (author only); the post page lists replies oldest first with a reply box, and the timeline shows reply counts.

features.name: Yasher koach: one reaction per person, optimistic in the interface
features.description: PUT/DELETE /api/v1/posts/{postId}/reaction, idempotent; the button changes state and count at once, rolls back and announces a refusal, and marks the pressed state with an icon and aria-pressed.

features.name: Notifications for follows, replies, reactions and new posts
features.description: Written in the action's transaction: a follow notifies the profile's owners, a reply or reaction the post's author, a post the profile's followers; never about one's own action.

features.name: The notifications list, unread count and the activity page
features.description: GET /api/v1/notifications (latest 50 and the unread count), POST /api/v1/notifications/read; an Activity link with an unread badge in social's nav, polled every 60 seconds; /social/notifications lists sentences that open their post or profile and marks everything read.

features.name: Share a post or a profile
features.description: A Share menu with Copy link, WhatsApp, Email and the browser's share sheet; the absolute link is built with host.href; Link copied is announced and focus returns to Share.

features.name: Open a source beside the feed
features.description: A post's source opens beside the page through contract 1.1 host.openBeside (the reader slides the text in and keeps the page mounted in a column); a 1.0 reader gets commands.go. The pages lay out by their own width (container queries), so they fit the column.

features.name: Repost a post
features.description: A profile reposts a post unchanged to its followers (one per profile per post, undoable); the network's reposts appear in Following with who reposted them; every post carries its repost count and whether the viewer reposted it.

features.name: Quote a post
features.description: A learner posts their own words carrying another post; the quoted post shows inside the quote (unavailable once deleted) and counts its quotes. The demo community has reposts and quotes.

features.name: For you: the timeline ranked like X's
features.description: The second tab ranks recent posts per viewer with X's heavy-ranker sum and published weights, a 24-hour half-life from the latest boost, out-of-network × 0.75 unless the network reposted it, and author diversity.

features.name: The conversation, ordered like X's
features.description: Replies under a post: the post's author's first, then from profiles the viewer follows, then the rest, oldest first within each.

features.name: Social page shows the surface name and contract version
features.description: The /social placeholder page shows the heading "Sefaria Social" and the line "Surface: social, SurfaceHost contract v1.0", from one constant in app/src/lib/surface-info.ts.

features.name: Pinned SurfaceHost contract with runtime schemas
features.description: packages/host-contract pins the reader's SurfaceHost v1 contract files with their source commit and hashes (pin check in L3), re-exports its types, and validates every value that crosses it with zod schemas proven equal to the pinned types.

features.name: Fake host for tests and the harness
features.description: An in-memory SurfaceHost typed from the pinned contract: browser-like history, refusal of off-site navigation, ctx exposure, snapshot apply that keeps ctx, test-key tokens, recorded calls.

features.name: Surface entry mounts into the reader page
features.description: The surface's default export mounts the page view (host-bridged router, R4) and the persistent view (renders only in a social ctx, R18); links go through the host (R15); never touches window.history (R1); a host from another major gets a reload notice.

features.name: Surface build with a release manifest
features.description: npm run build:surface emits an ES module entry, chunks, one CSS file and manifest.json in the reader's manifest format with sha384 hashes; the build refuses Start runtime and server imports.

features.name: Harness page loads the built surface into the fake host
features.description: harness/ is a fake reader page that loads the built surface through its manifest into the fake host over the browser's history, shows the reader's location, ctx, snapshot and the calls the surface made, and runs the L4a journeys.

features.name: Social settings page at /social/settings
features.description: Placeholder settings page with a tab in the search (?tab=profile|notifications), validated per route; unknown parameters dropped (R7).

features.name: Social's own not-found page
features.description: Any path under /social that is not an R6 page, or has an invalid id, renders social's not-found page inside the surface (R6).

features.name: SurfaceHost 1.2 chrome insets for the call window
features.description: The pinned contract is SurfaceHost 1.2 with an optional ui.chrome (the reader chrome insets); the call window keeps inside the viewport minus them and re-places when they change, falls back to a 64px top inset on an older reader, and reports bad values once. The fake host offers settable insets and a 1.1 variant.

features.name: One call and one room connection for both of the reader's mounts
features.description: The reader may give the page and persistent mounts different host objects; the call, room, sessions, recording, broadcast and replay controllers and the window owner are kept once per page (features/host/document-host.ts), so Join call in the lobby opens the call window and a room has one connection.

features.name: Sefaria identity token verified on every API call
features.description: Bearer RS256 tokens from Django verified with jose against the configured JWKS (issuer, audience sefaria-social, expiry, numeric sub); cached keys, refetch on unknown kid, 503 when the JWKS does not answer in 3 s.

features.name: Account deletion in Sefaria removes the user's social data
features.description: Signed user.deleted webhook from Django: HMAC verified over the raw body, idempotent on the event id, deletes the user's rows in one transaction and writes a tombstone that refuses their remaining tokens; a staff purge-user command; a walk-the-schema test.

features.name: Relay accepts only verified Sefaria tokens
features.description: Token from Sec-WebSocket-Protocol verified against the JWKS on upgrade; the token decides the participant's id and name.

features.name: Relay drops a deleted user
features.description: Internal drop-user call closes the user's sockets and refuses their upgrades for 30 minutes.

features.name: Account deletion drops the user from the relay
features.description: After the deletion webhook commits, the server asks the relay to drop the user from their rooms.

features.name: Test-only persona sessions
features.description: POST /api/test/persona (QA server only: SOCIAL_ENV ^test(-|$) and x-qa-persona-secret) returns a persona token and a one-time harness sign-in URL; GET /api/v1/me; never in the production build.

features.name: Person and institution profiles
features.description: GET/PATCH /api/v1/profiles/me (created on first use; name and bio; the institutions administered); settings' profile tab edits them and the composer offers Post as.

features.name: A profile page: kind, bio, counts, follow state and posts
features.description: GET /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}; /social/u/$profileId with a kind label, bio, counts, Follow (or Edit profile on one's own) and its posts.

features.name: One-tap follow
features.description: PUT/DELETE /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}/follow, idempotent, refusing to follow oneself; the button and count change at once.

features.name: Who to follow
features.description: GET /api/v1/profiles?suggested=1: up to 6 profiles not yet followed, institutions first, then the most followed people; shown in the feed's rail.

features.name: Postgres schema, migrations and a public health check
features.description: Seven tables (rooms, room_members, shiurim, shiur_recordings, user_display, deleted_users, webhook_receipts) from committed SQL migrations, timestamptz and indexed foreign keys, an expand/contract migration check, and GET /api/v1/health (public, database only, 503 within 2 s when it does not answer).

features.name: Structured request logs with a correlation id
features.description: One JSON log line per API request (static message, method, route template, status, duration, correlation id), never headers, bodies or tokens; X-Correlation-Id propagated or generated.

features.name: Surface bundle size budget checked in CI
features.description: The surface build is fully minified (rolldown output.minify; no pure annotations), and `npm run surface:budget` checks the files the manifest lists (raw and gzip) against app/surface-budget.json in CI's build job, failing with the fix when a budget is exceeded.

features.name: Release pipeline with versioned assets, a stable pointer and rollback
features.description: `npm run release -- publish|promote|rollback|status|smoke|serve` over a storage target (file:<dir> works; bucket:<name> is a stub until hosting exists): immutable uploads under v/<version>/, a smoke-tested stable/manifest.json pointer with known-good history, scripts/rollback, release.yml on main (rehearsal on a folder; real steps skip with a notice without their configuration), and an e2e release and rollback through the harness.

features.name: Server container image and standalone Helm values
features.description: A pinned, non-root Dockerfile with a /api/v1/health HEALTHCHECK running app/scripts/start.mjs (and app/scripts/migrate.mjs), its rules checked by `release check-dockerfile`, CI's container job running the image against Postgres, and deploy/helm/values.yaml for a standalone namespace.

features.name: Coolify deployment with a preview per pull request
features.description: docker-compose.yaml builds app (the server, migrating before it serves), surface (the release build behind nginx, no-cache manifest, immutable assets, any origin), relay (the Worker in workerd from its environment) and postgres; one Coolify app is the shared dev backend and builds a full preview per pull request.

features.name: Agent lanes skip with a notice when credentials are absent
features.description: Review, QA, security, retro and holdout lanes run factory/preflight.mjs first; with no Anthropic credential (or on a fork, or for a bot) they skip with a notice naming the missing secret, and never fail a PR for it.

features.name: Agent jobs are capped, gated and hold no deploy credentials
features.description: factory doctor fails when an agent job lacks a time limit, a turn limit, a model, a tool list, a preflight gate, fork refusal or a pinned action, or reads any secret beyond the Anthropic key and the workflow token; workflows are linted by actionlint and doctor.

features.name: QA surfaces derived from the diff through the surface map
features.description: npm run factory -- surfaces maps changed files to QA surfaces through factory/surface-map.yaml (shared code to every importer); an unmapped product file fails; doctor checks spec and atlas surfaces exist in the map.

features.name: QA recount applies what a pass means
features.description: npm run factory -- qa-recount counts the runner evidence: retries are failed-then-recovered, unreachable surfaces cannot-reach, passes need an evidence line; a surface with no journey blocks the report.

features.name: Agent QA lane posts one evidence comment
features.description: agent-qa.yml builds the environment in the job (Postgres service, qa:* scripts), runs planner, runner and skeptic as separate agents, and posts one evidence comment and one issue per failure.

features.name: CI appends metrics lines to the factory-data branch
features.description: factory/metrics.mjs validates JSON lines and appends them to factory-data metrics/YYYY-MM.jsonl (created as an orphan branch by the first workflow write); ci.yml metrics job and the composite action write one line per job.

features.name: Quality score generated per surface
features.description: npm run factory -- quality-score writes docs/QUALITY_SCORE.md (test files per level per surface); --check fails when it is stale; the nightly publishes the version with flake and escaped-defect columns.

features.name: Nightly flake detection over three runs
features.description: nightly.yml runs every suite three times and lists tests with mixed results; also mutation, audit, contract drift, docs freshness and doctor; e2e-reader.yml (L4b) is disabled until the reader seam lands.

features.name: Collection check: test files on disk equal files executed
features.description: npm run factory -- collection fails when a test file on disk was not executed by any runner, per level.

features.name: Quarantine list with reason, issue and expiry
features.description: factory/quarantine.yaml entries need a reason, an issue link and an expiry within 30 days; expired entries fail; a quarantined failure is a notice, any other failure fails.

features.name: Weekly retro numbers from the metrics store
features.description: npm run factory -- retro computes the week numbers, past action items and recurring problems from factory-data; retro.yml publishes them weekly and runs the retro agent behind its preflight.

features.name: Holdout scenarios scored from three clean trials
features.description: npm run factory -- holdout validates scenario files, scores three clean trials (pass, fail or unknown per rubric line) and writes issue bodies with scenario text redacted; nightly.yml checks out the holdout repo with a deploy key and skips with a notice until it exists.

features.name: Idempotent QA seed and schema-checked reset
features.description: npm run qa:seed creates nothing the second time; npm run qa:reset leaves zero rows in every table the schema lists.

features.name: Demo content: a seeded community for the first visit
features.description: npm run qa:seed -- demo seeds invented institutions, people, posts with sources, replies, reactions, follows and notifications, idempotently; --for <userId> makes a real account follow the institutions and run the first.

features.name: Call chunk budget
features.description: The LiveKit call chunk (assets/call.*.js) has its own gzip limit and is left out of the surface totals; the entry may grow at most 4 kB over its size before calls.

features.name: Two-browser call journey on a local LiveKit
features.description: The e2e stack runs LiveKit in development mode; two Chromium contexts with fake cameras join one room call on desktop and phone: video and audio arrive, mute shows, the call survives moving, leaving keeps the room.

features.name: Room lobby page at /social/r/$roomId
features.description: Placeholder room lobby page; ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}$ (R6).

features.name: Create, list, rename and delete rooms with ownership checks
features.description: POST/GET /api/v1/rooms and GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/rooms/{roomId}; members read, owners rename and delete, non-members get 404, invalid input 400.

features.name: Join and leave a room from its link
features.description: POST /api/v1/rooms/{roomId}/members joins (the room id is the invitation); DELETE .../members/me leaves.

features.name: Presence list
features.description: Who is in the room, live: name, leading, following whom, away; the viewer marked as you.

features.name: Lobby Join button
features.description: A non-member on /social/r/<id> sees Join; signed-out viewers are sent to sign in.

features.name: N on a call in the lobby and on cards
features.description: The lobby and room cards say how many are on the room call while one is live; the room status and the feed carry call only then.

features.name: Start a room from Social and land in its lobby
features.description: Start a room on the home rail, the rooms page and empty states: a dialog asks for the name (required, at most 120 characters), creates the room and opens its lobby; a failure keeps the dialog open. The rail also links to all rooms, and a recording's page links back to its room.

features.name: Your rooms at /social/rooms and Rooms in Social's navigation
features.description: Every room the viewer is a member of, newest first, with Owner or Member and a link to its lobby; empty and signed-out states; a one-shot notice after a room is deleted or left.

features.name: Invite people from a room's lobby: its link with Copy and Share
features.description: A member's lobby says whether they own the room and shows Invite people: the room's full link, Copy (announced), and the Share menu.

features.name: Rename or delete a room you own
features.description: Room settings in the lobby: the owner renames the room in place, or deletes it after a confirmation that says its recordings go too, then lands on the rooms page with a notice.

features.name: Leave a room you joined
features.description: A member who is not the owner leaves the room from room settings after a confirmation; the session of that room in this browser closes first; the rooms page says so.

features.name: The lobby says when calls are off
features.description: Where Join call would be, the lobby says video calls are not turned on when the server does not offer them.

features.name: Social context in the reader's ctx parameter
features.description: app/src/lib/ctx.ts encodes and decodes social.room.<id> / social.shiur.<id> and adds or removes only social's ctx on a reader URL, keeping every other parameter byte for byte (R3, R11).

features.name: Enlarge and minimise session state machine
features.description: app/src/features/session/machine.ts: the SessionView union of plan 4.3 with an explicit transition table; illegal moves are refused and leave the state unchanged.

features.name: Room protocol and client in packages/session
features.description: The room (validation, limits, spotlight, streams) and the session client (follow through the state API, publish when needed), started from the reader's src/lib/session.

features.name: Relay: one Durable Object per room in the Workers runtime
features.description: Worker and Durable Object from the reader's relay running packages/session's room; Origin and path checks.

features.name: Enlarge into a room's reader context
features.description: R9 and R10: own place kept, target snapshot, push with ctx, apply on context ready; streamed moves replace; Back leaves.

features.name: Follow, follow again and lead
features.description: Following the spotlight or a picked participant through applySnapshot; breaking away and coming back; taking the lead.

features.name: Protocol fixtures keep social's and the reader's copies in step
features.description: Recorded protocol results from the reader's room code, replayed against packages/session; a drift check against a reader checkout.

features.name: Relay status read for cards
features.description: Internal status of a room: ref and title from the spotlight stream's summary slice and the participant count.

features.name: Minimise to the own place or the lobby
features.description: R12: push the own place without ctx or the lobby; the persistent mount shows the mini view.

features.name: Reconnect from ctx alone on a cold load
features.description: R11: the persistent mount connects from the ctx value alone.

features.name: Nothing personal applied or sent
features.description: R13 and R14: only the viewer's moment slices are applied; outgoing snapshots lose ctx, personal slices and search words, and gain the summary slice.

features.name: Two learners in one room on the harness
features.description: P3's exit journey in Playwright with two browser contexts, a local relay and server.

features.name: Stream summary carries heRef and the source's title
features.description: social.summary = {ref, heRef, title}; heRef and title from the text API's answer, republished when it lands; the relay status read and the server pass heRef on.

features.name: Enlarging from a card lands on its source without a reload
features.description: End to end on the harness: the applied snapshot's ref equals the card's, the document is not reloaded, Back returns to the feed.

features.name: Calls switch and the room's calls field
features.description: Calls are available only with LIVEKIT_URL, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET set and CALLS_ENABLED=true; otherwise the token request is 503 call.unavailable. Every room response carries calls.available.

features.name: Call state machine and controller
features.description: One call per tab, tied to a room session: pre-join, connecting, in call, reconnecting with a fresh token (30 s, then Rejoin), ended. Leaving the call keeps the room; leaving the room ends the call first. Reports carry no personal data.

features.name: Join a call with devices off, and talk
features.description: Join call in the lobby and the follow bar when calls are available; a pre-join step with microphone and camera off, device choosers and a preview; denied permission still lets you listen; tiles, microphone, camera and screen share controls.

features.name: Calls load on demand and survive reading
features.description: No LiveKit code, connection or device request before Join call; the call stays connected through every in-reader navigation; a reload offers Join call and never rejoins by itself.

features.name: Floating call window: place, move, resize
features.description: The call floats over the reader in a fixed window, top inline-end by default; sizes pill, small, medium, large; dragged by its handle and snapped to a corner; resized within limits; kept on screen; its place remembered; hidden tiles send no video. The text column never moves.

features.name: Call window by keyboard and screen reader
features.description: Arrow keys move the window from its handle, a menu offers corners and sizes, moves are announced politely, Escape collapses to the pill without trapping focus, controls are 24 px with focus rings and names, and reduced motion turns animation off.

features.name: The call on a phone: a docked strip
features.description: Below 600px the call is a full-width strip under the top inset: 48px collapsed (avatars, speaking, microphone, Leave, Expand; no video received), the active speaker at 16:9 when expanded. Rotating switches between strip and window without touching the call. After the browser pauses a background tab, one Resume button restarts audio.

features.name: Owner tile menu, and what the muted and removed see
features.description: An owner sees a menu on every other tile (mute microphone, turn off camera, stop screen share, remove); the muted are told the host muted them and can unmute; the removed are told so and stay in the room.

features.name: Record a room's session (state and call media) in the owner's browser
features.description: The room's owner records a session from the call: their browser mixes the call's audio, composes its video and records the reader's state stream beside it, uploading both as it goes, while everyone in the room sees a Recording badge in the lobby and the call window.

features.name: Replay a recording in the reader with the video in the floating window
features.description: A room's ready recordings are listed in its lobby and have their own page (Play, Download state, Delete for the recorder or the room's owner); Play opens the reader at the recording's first text in its context with the video in the floating call window (the strip on a phone), whose transport drives the media and the reader together, and the call and a replay never share the window.

features.name: Broadcast a session and watch it as a view-only viewer
features.description: A room's owner presses Broadcast in the lobby to publish their reader to a broadcast relay room (b_<id>) holding the spotlight, with a link to copy, the number watching, the broadcast's call and End broadcast; anyone signed in with the link presses Watch on /social/b/<id> to follow the host in the reader with ctx=social.watch.<id> (breaking away, then Back to live) and see and hear the host view only, until "The broadcast has ended".

features.name: Stay in the room while reading around the reader
features.description: A reader page reached without ctx while in a room (a link, a search) gets the room's ctx back with a replace, so the viewer stays in the room; Back to where they entered from, a Social page or another room still leaves.

features.name: The room window in the reader: a card with the room, its status and who is here
features.description: The follow bar and mini view as one card at the bottom inline-start corner: title and live dot, status, Follow again or Lead, Join call, who is here with Follow, the room's page, Minimise; folds into a pill for the session.

features.name: The call window looks like a call: tiles, initials, an icon control bar, a real pre-join
features.description: Dark 16:10 tiles with the camera or the person's initials, a name label with a muted mark and a speaking ring; one row of round icon buttons with names and on/off states and a red Leave call; the pre-join step's preview with its toggles, Join and Cancel on it.

features.name: Sticky following: break away only by a clear move
features.description: Input alone never pauses a follower: once the reader is still for 400 ms its place is compared with the followed person's, and only another book or section, or 5 or more segments away, sets them on their own.

features.name: The room's owner is its one leader
features.description: The server signs a room relay ticket naming the caller as owner or member; the relay makes only an owner ticket a host who may lead, so members cannot take the spotlight, and the room window offers no Lead button.

features.name: Follow a person by clicking them; the leader takes followers along
features.description: Clicking a person in who is here or on their call tile follows them, clicking again returns to the leader, a leader who follows someone gets Lead again, and moves the leader takes from someone they follow reach the leader's followers.

features.name: Shiur page at /social/s/$shiurId
features.description: Placeholder shiur page with a link to a ref through the reader's workspace commands (R15).
